situation: On holiday in Kribi, Maïmouna builds a sandcastle near the water. The waves reach the beach at an angle, and the water flows straight back to the sea.
After an hour, she sees that some sand from her castle has moved along the beach. She wonders where the sand of the beach comes from, and what moves it along the coast.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that Maïmouna does not know where the sand comes from and what moves it along the coast.
How do the waves reach the beach?
They reach the beach at an angle, and the water flows straight back.
Why is it bad to take too much sand from beaches for building?
Without sand, the beach cannot protect the land, and the waves erode the coast faster.
end.justification: This lesson will help us to understand how waves move and deposit sand to build beaches, spits, bars and tombolos.

qa.a: Longshore drift is the movement of sand and pebbles along the coast by waves that reach the beach at an angle.

qa.q: Explain how longshore drift moves sand.
qa.a: The swash carries sand up the beach at an angle. The backwash brings it straight back down. This zig-zag moves the sand along the coast.

sum.title: I. Longshore Drift
defs: Longshore drift is the movement of sand and pebbles along the coast by waves that reach the beach at an angle.
items: The Steps
– The wind makes waves reach the beach at an angle.
– The swash carries sand up the beach at the same angle.
– The backwash brings the sand straight back down.
– The zig-zag movement slowly moves the sand along the coast.
longshore_spit.png

qa.a: A beach is a deposit of sand and pebbles between the low-tide and the high-tide marks. Examples: the beaches of Kribi and Limbe.
Where the coast changes direction, longshore drift keeps depositing sand into the sea. A long, narrow ridge grows, attached to the land at one end.

qa.title: Question 3
qa.q: What is the difference between a bar and a tombolo?
qa.a: A bar is a ridge of sand across a bay; it traps a lagoon behind it. A tombolo is a ridge of sand that joins an island to the land.

sum.title: II. Depositional Features
sum.intro: Wave deposition forms the following features:
items: A. Beaches
A beach is a deposit of sand and pebbles between the low-tide and high-tide marks (Kribi, Limbe).
B. Spits
A spit is a long, narrow ridge of sand joined to the land at one end, built by longshore drift where the coast changes direction (Langue de Barbarie, Senegal).
longshore_spit.png
C. Bars and Lagoons
A bar is a ridge of sand that grows across a bay and traps a lagoon behind it (lagoons of Lagos and Abidjan).
bar_tombolo.png
D. Tombolos
A tombolo is a ridge of sand that joins an island to the mainland.

evaluation: It is the movement of sand along the coast by waves that reach the beach at an angle.
A spit is a long, narrow ridge of sand attached to the land at one end.
What is trapped behind a bar?
A lagoon is trapped behind a bar.
remediation: The movement of sand along the coast is longshore ______.
The swash moves sand up the beach at an ______.
A ridge of sand joined to the land at one end is a ______.
A ridge of sand across a bay is a ______.
The water trapped behind a bar is a ______.
A ridge of sand joining an island to the land is a ______.
end.remediationAnswers: 1. drift 2. angle 3. spit 4. bar 5. lagoon 6. tombolo
